newsitem.title: USA: Boeing steps up merger talks with EU.
newsitem.headline: Boeing steps up merger talks with EU.

text.p: Boeing Co has sent a delegation of high-level executives to Brussels for intensified negotiations with European Union officials over the company's planned $14 billion acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp.
Boeing spokeswoman Sherry Nebel said the latest talks aimed at overcoming EU opposition to the merger began Friday and were expected to continue through the weekend.

Although the EU's deadline for making a final decision on the merger is not until July 23, this weekend is considered crucial because of the need to prepare, translate and distribute documents to European Commission members.

Lower-level Boeing and McDonnell Douglas officials have been holding discussions with EC staff members since July 4, when competition experts from the alliance's 15-member countries unanimously recommended that the merger be blocked in its current form.
The competition experts rejected unspecified remedies being offered by Boeing to overcome European objections to the merger, leaving the Seattle-based aerospace company to modify its proposals.

Nebel declined to identify the Boeing executives involved in the latest round of talks, but the Seattle Post-Intelligencer newspaper reported the latest delegation included Richard Albrecht and Dick Pearson of Boeing's commercial airplane group, corporate attorney Douglas Bain and an outside attorney, Tom Boeder.

Although the U.S. Federal Trade Commission has approved the Boeing merger unconditionally, the EU also claims jurisdiction because both companies have significant business interests in Europe. While the European Commission technically cannot block the deal, it could seek to impose penalties of up to 10 percent of Boeing's gross revenues if the company completes a merger over its objections.
